  "question_intent": "Valuation of business plans",
  "main_topics": ["Business Valuation", "Asia Business Plan", "Capital Funding", "Liquidity Implications", "Risk Appetite", "Growth Acceleration", "Synergies", "Re-rating", "De-rating", "Structural Alternatives"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Hedged",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": false,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "And valuations.",
  "answer_quote": "Could you imagine a different business plan for Asia? Yes, you could, Manus, but you would have to work through all of the capital funding, liquidity implications and risk appetite implications of that. There's been some suggestions that we could accelerate growth in some areas, but that would come with a change risk appetite and therefore change capital funding and liquidity implications that we've started to work through, but again, we think the overall net de-synergies outweigh any of those positive synergies. Yes, you could speculate that there could be a re-rating of the Asian business if it was separated out it. Equally, we think there would be a de-rating of the rest of the world, so when we've looked at those two together, we haven't been able to convince ourselves that there's some kind of magic structural alternative that delivers a re-rating for the overall group.",
  "reason": "The answer addresses the question of valuations and discusses various factors such as business plans, capital funding, and risk appetite, but it does not provide specific numeric evidence or forward guidance."
}
